name: The agent as an economic actor
oneLine: Discovers, pays, proves and gets rated; the machine persona.
goals: Discover a service, read its price and payment requirements, and pay within one request cycle.
Hold a stable identity (an agentId, a signing key, a registration) that counterparties can look up before accepting a request.
Stay inside the budget, payee list and expiry of the mandate it was given, and halt when a constraint fails.
Produce receipts and proofs (transaction hashes, a Payment-Receipt, signed mandates) for every payment so its principal and auditors can verify them.
Accumulate feedback that raises its probability of being selected for the next task.
Pay other agents for subtasks using the same protocols it accepts payments through.
pains: Services speak x402 V1, x402 V2 or MPP, and a wrong guess costs a round trip or a failed payment.
A payment can settle and the service can still fail or return unusable output. The exact scheme has no refund path, and most flows have no evaluator.
Edge verification requires a key in a vendor directory the agent may not be listed in, so verified-only merchants return 403 or a block page.
Feedback is written by counterparties and cannot be contested beyond appendResponse, while Sybil reviewers dilute honest scores.
Mandates from different providers (AP2, Verifiable Intent, an SPT allowance) carry the same constraints in different shapes, and an unrecognized constraint must cause a hard failure.
Prompt injection in a merchant page or a tool result can redirect the agent's payment, and the agent has no independent check on its own instructions.
decisions: Which service to buy from when several quote a price, given cost, reputation and proof of past payment.
Whether to pay upfront, by authorization, or by opening a session, based on the expected task length.
When to stop and request a new mandate instead of continuing within an expiring or exhausted one.
Which identity to present (agentId, Web Bot Auth key, registered agent credential) for a given counterparty.
